definition: Of, relating to, or determined by the stars; used especially to describe time or motion measured with reference to the distant stars rather than the sun.
etymology: From Latin sidereus, starry, itself from sidus (genitive sideris), a star or constellation. The Romans borrowed the root from an older Indo-European sense of gleaming or glittering. It arrived in English in the seventeenth century just as astronomers needed precise language to distinguish star-time from sun-time.
usage: On this June night, when dusk lingers longest and the stars take their time appearing, a sidereal reckoning reminds us that the clock we live by and the clock the cosmos keeps are never quite the same thing.
